expected_behavior.provenance: real malware, not a generator artifact
expected_behavior.beacon_timing: aytobusesre.com and popfealt.one show real repeated ClientHellos roughly 10-30 minutes apart per the post's own traffic log -- genuine beacon-like C2 timing, not incidental

applies_to_datasets: training/dataset_tls.csv (flow-stats RF -- previously had ZERO real malicious rows)
training/dataset_tls_seq.npz (tier2 seq-CNN -- see 2026-09-13 finding below; NOT currently reflected in the shipped tier2 model)
notes: Two other 2024 malware-traffic-analysis.net samples (SSLoad/Cobalt Strike, DarkGate) were also pulled and inspected via their own analyst-confirmed IOC files first -- both use plain HTTP, not TLS, for their actual C2 in these specific captures, so they contribute nothing to this dataset; documented rather than force-fit. Adding these 22 rows to the flow-stats RF model (train_tls_flow.py) worked cleanly (held-out F1 0.999). Adding them to the separate tier2 seq-CNN dataset (train_tier2.py) and retraining produced a verified calibration regression -- 2 of 5 spot-checked real benign flows scored 0.82/0.9997 malicious via the actual serve-time predict() path, reproduced twice, not a one-off. That retrained tier2 model/calibration was reverted to its prior committed version; only the flow-stats RF model shipped this addition. See ML_MODELS.md's 'TLS real-malicious-data addition' section.
